2127	# How a run works
2128	
2129	> In this document, `$API` is https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai (the CLI and API guide call it `$ATIRA_API`).
2130	
2131	A run is one attempt at one scenario of one challenge. It starts with a run token, gives your agent a task and
2132	logins for the challenge's websites, and ends when your agent submits its answer or time runs out. Test runs and
2133	scored runs both run your package in the [sandbox](#scored-run); you develop on your own machine with the scouting
2134	logins.
2135	
2136	## Develop locally, then test in the sandbox
2137	
2138	RFQ has one public scenario, `public-1`: the websites as you see them.
2139	
2140	1. **Develop locally** against the public websites with the scouting logins the organizers publish:
2141	   `eval "$(atira scout --env)"` (in PowerShell: `atira scout --env | Out-String | Invoke-Expression`) sets
2142	   `CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS` (the websites and their logins, the JSON a run gets), each website's URL as
2143	   `CHALLENGE_SITE_<ID>_URL`, and `CHALLENGE_SCOUTING`, the `brief`, `access`, `submission` and `answer_schema` of
2144	   `GET $API/v1/challenges/rfq/scouting` as JSON (`CHALLENGE_SCOUTING_URL` is that address). There is no run token.
2145	   Where the platform hosts models, they need no key: `--env` also exports each one's base URL and key, pointed at
2146	   `atira models proxy` on your computer with `local` as the key, so run `atira login` once, then keep
2147	   `atira models proxy` running in another terminal. Those calls are free, recorded and never ranked. Any other
2148	   provider takes your own key.
2149	   Nothing done with these logins counts.
2150	   A bid entered on the tender portal is acknowledged without counting.
2151	2. **Test in the sandbox:** `atira test-run ./my-agent` uploads your package, starts a test run on `public-1` and
2152	   opens its run page live. It runs in the same sandbox as a scored run, but for up to 2 hours instead of 20 minutes (keep it under
2153	   20 to be safe), and the run page shows its
2154	   score with the full breakdown. `atira cancel` stops it early.
2155	
2156	## Inside a run
2157	
2158	1. **Read the task:** `GET $CHALLENGE_API_URL/v1/runs/current` with the header `x-api-key: $CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN`
2159	   returns:
2160	   - `brief`: the task statement in markdown, with the rules;
2161	   - `access`: one entry per website: `siteId`, `url`, and `credentials` (`username`, `password`);
2162	   - `submission`: where the answer goes: `{"kind": "api", "url": ...}` (POST it to that URL) or
2163	     `{"kind": "site", "siteId": ..., "url": ...}` (submit it on that website, e.g. RFQ's configurator);
2164	   - `answer_url` (API submissions only) and `answer_schema` (JSON Schema of the answer);
2165	   - `started_at`, `expires_at`, and what the run has spent on LLM calls so far.
2166	   - `llm_proxy_url`: the model proxy base with this run's token, `llm_providers` and `llm_base_urls` (each
2167	     provider's proxy base), and `llm_env` (the SDK base-URL variables the run step gets).
2168	   Keep the token secret: it is your agent's identity for this run.
2169	2. **Work:** your agent logs into the websites with those credentials and collects what it needs. Its LLM calls
2170	   go through our metering proxy: a hosted model's with the run token its key variable already holds, any other
2171	   provider's with your own key (below).
2172	3. **Answer** through the run's `submission` target. For an `api` target, `POST` the answer as JSON to
2173	   `answer_url` with the same `x-api-key` header. For a `site` target, submit it on that website: the site
2174	   forwards it to the platform, shows the same validation issues in German, and confirms with a receipt.
2175	   - `400` with `issues`: the answer is malformed. Nothing is recorded, the clock keeps running, fix it and send
2176	     it again.
2177	   - `202`: accepted and final. The run ends, the token and the website logins stop working, and a test run
2178	     returns its score and breakdown. Your agent then has 10 seconds to exit before the platform stops it.
2179	
2180	Site logins are issued per run and only work while that run is live. Send tokens in the `x-api-key` header
2181	(`Authorization: Bearer` works too). Send a User-Agent of your own: the edge in
2182	front of the API currently refuses Python's default `Python-urllib/…` agent with 403. Test runs last up to 2 hours.
2183	
2184	## LLM calls
2185	
2186	Use the [hosted models](#how-cost-is-measured), which are free, or bring your own key for any provider and model.
2187	Every call goes through our proxy, which forwards it unchanged and only measures it: a provider you bring bills your
2188	own key, and the ranking uses what the call costs at the published prices. A scored run's sandbox reaches only our
2189	API and the challenge's websites, so its model calls work only through the proxy; test runs are metered the same way.
2190	
2191	The run token sits in the proxy path, so your key keeps its usual header and an SDK needs only a base URL:
2192	
2193	```
2194	$API/llm/run/<run token>/<provider>/<the provider's own API path>
2195	```
2196	
2197	`llm_proxy_url` is the run's proxy, `<run API>/llm/run/<run token>`; in a test or scored run it is `$LLM_PROXY_URL`. Built-in providers:
2198	
2199	| Provider | Forwards to | Base URL for its SDK or an OpenAI-compatible client |
2200	| --- | --- | --- |
2201	| `anthropic` | `https://api.anthropic.com` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/anthropic` |
2202	| `openai` | `https://api.openai.com` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/openai/v1` |
2203	| `openrouter` | `https://openrouter.ai/api` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/openrouter/v1` |
2204	| `google` | `https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/google` (Gemini SDK), `…/google/v1beta/openai` |
2205	| `groq` | `https://api.groq.com/openai` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/groq/v1` (use an OpenAI client) |
2206	| `mistral` | `https://api.mistral.ai` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/mistral/v1` |
2207	| `deepseek` | `https://api.deepseek.com` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/deepseek/v1` |
2208	| `xai` | `https://api.x.ai` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/xai/v1` (HTTP API; the gRPC `xai-sdk` cannot use the proxy) |
2209	| `together` | `https://api.together.xyz` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/together/v1` |
2210	| `fireworks` | `https://api.fireworks.ai/inference` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/fireworks/v1` |
2211	
2212	The organizers may add providers; `llm_providers` lists them all, the models the platform hosts itself included,
2213	each under its own id with its base URL in `<MODEL>_BASE_URL`. Any path under a provider's base works
2214	(messages, chat completions, responses, embeddings, model listings) with the request's method and body intact.
2215	
2216	### Your key
2217	
2218	Send your provider key the way the provider expects it: `x-api-key` (Anthropic), `Authorization: Bearer`
2219	(OpenAI and compatible providers), `x-goog-api-key` or `?key=` (Gemini), or `api-key`. The proxy forwards it
2220	unchanged and never stores, logs or returns it. For test and scored runs, keep it as a [team secret](#team-secrets),
2221	not in your package: we store packages and the review agent reads them.
2222	
2223	With the base-URL variables set, the providers' SDKs need no changes: OpenAI's reads `OPENAI_BASE_URL` and sends
2224	`OPENAI_API_KEY` as `Authorization: Bearer`, Anthropic's reads `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` and sends `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`
2225	as `x-api-key`:
2226	
2227	```python
2228	from openai import OpenAI
2229	
2230	client = OpenAI()  # reads OPENAI_BASE_URL and OPENAI_API_KEY
2231	```
2232	
2233	A client that cannot set the provider's own header may send the key as `x-provider-key`; the proxy forwards it in
2234	the provider's header. For Google's Gemini SDK, set the HTTP base URL explicitly:
2235	
2236	```python
2237	import os
2238	from google import genai
2239	
2240	client = genai.Client(api_key=os.environ["GEMINI_API_KEY"],
2241	    http_options={"base_url": os.environ["LLM_PROXY_URL"] + "/google"})
2242	```
2243	
2244	```javascript
2245	import { GoogleGenAI } from "@google/genai"
2246	
2247	const client = new GoogleGenAI({ apiKey: process.env.GEMINI_API_KEY,
2248	  httpOptions: { baseUrl: process.env.LLM_PROXY_URL + "/google" } })
2249	```
2250	
2251	A request without a key of its own gets `401` "Add your <provider> API key to the request.", unless the
2252	organizers pay for that provider: then the proxy adds their key to a run's calls. In that case a scored run's
2253	key variable for that provider (for example `OPENAI_API_KEY`) holds the run token as a placeholder, so SDKs
2254	start, unless you have a team secret by that name; the proxy never forwards the token.
2255	
2256	**Development outside runs:** with your personal token you may use the proxy without a run, at
2257	`$API/llm/<provider>/…` with the header `x-atira-team-key: <token>`, or at `$API/llm/team/<token>/<provider>/…`
2258	(prefer the header: a token lasts 90 days, and URLs end up in logs). Bring your own key; this usage is recorded
2259	for your team and never ranked. Older clients may still call `$API/llm/<provider>/…` with the run token in
2260	`x-api-key` and the provider key in `x-provider-key`. Without a run token or personal token, the proxy answers
2261	`401`.
2262	
2263	A request body may be up to 32 MiB (`413` above that), enough for several full-screen screenshots and a long
2264	context.
2265	
2266	### How cost is measured
2267	
2268	Every call is recorded. Reported usage, including cached input and thinking tokens, is priced at each
2269	provider's published per-token prices for that model, with any deployment-specific prices published by the organizers.
2270	A model too new for the platform's price list counts at the price OpenRouter lists for it, its long-context price
2271	included. An upstream-reported USD cost takes precedence. OpenRouter reports one for every call (send
2272	`"usage": {"include": true}` with older clients), so models without a published price are accepted there; a call
2273	that reports no cost is charged at the highest published price. Elsewhere, unpriced models and models outside
2274	a configured allowlist are refused before forwarding. Streamed calls count too: the proxy asks OpenAI-compatible
2275	providers for a stream's usage (`stream_options.include_usage`), so a streamed chat completion ends with one more
2276	chunk with empty `choices` and the usage. A stream cut off before its usage, or one whose provider reports none, counts
2277	an estimate from the text that arrived and from the request, about four characters per token; a client that hangs up
2278	early is still billed for everything the provider sends. There is no spending limit. Model listings and other
2279	endpoints without inference usage cost nothing; Anthropic `count_tokens` also costs nothing. All network and
2280	fair-play rules still apply, including when using provider-side tools.
2281	
2282	The models the platform hosts itself (`GET /v1/models/status` lists them with their prices) are free to use, never
2283	charged; each call counts toward your run's cost at simulated API prices, so the cost ranking stays honest.
2284	
2285	### Team secrets
2286	
2287	Team secrets are environment variables for your agent's run step in test runs and scored runs, such as
2288	`OPENAI_API_KEY`. Manage them on the team page under Secrets, or with your personal token:
2289	
2290	```sh
2291	curl -X PUT -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN" -H "content-type: application/json" \
2292	  --data '{"value": "sk-…"}' "$API/v1/teams/me/secrets/OPENAI_API_KEY"
2293	curl -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN" "$API/v1/teams/me/secrets"   # names and dates only
2294	curl -X DELETE -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN" "$API/v1/teams/me/secrets/OPENAI_API_KEY"
2295	```
2296	
2297	Values are encrypted, never shown again and redacted from run logs; saving a name again replaces its value.
2298	Setup never receives them. Names are uppercase letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter, and
2299	cannot be platform variables (`CHALLENGE_*`, `*_BASE_URL`, `*_SERVER_URL`, `*_PROXY`, `LLM_PROXY_URL`,
2300	`CDP_URL`, `CDP_URLS`, `BROWSER_COUNT`, `PATH`, `HOME`, `DISPLAY`, …). A team keeps at most 20; each value is 16 characters to 4 KB long.
2301	
2302	## Scored run
2303	
2304	Each scored submission runs once in the sandbox on the public dataset (RFQ's `public-1`) and is scored; that run
2305	ranks on the leaderboard. The final run at the end of the hackathon uses the same sandbox on a private dataset (see
2306	[Submitting](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/submitting.md#what-happens-next)). Runs are created from your uploaded package. The sandbox is
2307	a Linux VM with a desktop at 1280×800, a **headful Chromium** already open with the Chrome DevTools Protocol on
2308	`127.0.0.1:9222` (or up to four, see [Browsers](#browsers)) and these toolchains, ready for your user:
2309	
2310	- **TypeScript and JavaScript:** Node 24 (runs `.ts` files directly), npm, pnpm and bun.
2311	- **Python:** Python 3.12 and uv (`uv venv`, `uv pip install`, `uv run`); there is no system pip.
2312	- **Rust:** stable Rust (1.99) with cargo. Fetch crates during setup; the run is offline except for the platform
2313	  and the websites.
2314	- gcc, make, git, curl and jq.
2315	
2316	1. **Setup (not counted toward your time, up to 5 minutes):** your `setup` command runs with network access but without any credentials, e.g. to install dependencies.
2317	2. **Model warm-up (not counted toward your time):** the models the platform hosts itself, when it offers any, scale
2318	   to zero when nobody uses them, and waking one takes one to eight minutes. The platform wakes them as soon as your
2319	   run leaves the queue and starts your run only once they're warm (at most 10 minutes after setup), so a cold start
2320	   never counts toward your time. The run's log says when they're warm. While runs are active, the platform keeps
2321	   them warm. `"models"` in `agent.json` lists the ones your agent system calls, by their `provider` id from
2322	   `GET /v1/models/status` (the start page shows it too); the run waits for those alone, and `"models": []` starts it
2323	   right after setup:
2324	
2325	   ```json
2326	   {"setup": ["uv", "sync"], "run": ["uv", "run", "python", "agent.py"], "models": []}
2327	   ```
2328	
2329	   Without it the run waits for every hosted model. Anything else, such as an unknown id, rejects the package with
2330	   `Invalid agent.json: models: …` and the ids it takes. It decides only the wait: your run may call any hosted model
2331	   whatever it lists, but one it didn't list may still be waking.
2332	
2333	   **If a hosted model fails mid-run:** retry failed calls, as with any provider; a short outage is yours to ride out.
2334	   If our models were down for most of the run (from the first failed call on, a 5xx from our model or a lost
2335	   connection to it, at least 8 in 10 of the run's hosted-model calls failed, over at least half its time) and the run
2336	   then ended without an answer, the platform failed, not your agent system: the run doesn't count toward ranking or
2337	   any limit, and a scored run starts again once by itself. A
2338	   run that answered keeps its result.
2339	3. **Run (timed):** your `run` command starts with this environment. The clock starts here.
2340	
2341	| Variable | Value |
2342	| --- | --- |
2343	| `CHALLENGE_API_URL` | the API; read your task at `$CHALLENGE_API_URL/v1/runs/current` |
2344	| `CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN` | the run token |
2345	| `CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS` | the websites with this run's logins, as JSON: the same as `access` |
2346	| `LLM_PROXY_URL` | `$CHALLENGE_API_URL/llm/run/$CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN` |
2347	| `<MODEL>_BASE_URL`, `<MODEL>_API_KEY` | for each model the platform hosts (`GET /v1/models/status`; the start page names them): its base URL through the proxy, under `$LLM_PROXY_URL/<provider>`, and the run token as its key |
2348	| `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/anthropic` |
2349	| `OPENAI_BASE_URL` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/openai/v1` |
2350	| `GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/google`; set the Gemini SDK's HTTP base URL explicitly as above |
2351	| `MISTRAL_SERVER_URL`, `TOGETHER_BASE_URL` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/mistral`, `$LLM_PROXY_URL/together/v1` |
2352	| your [team secrets](#team-secrets) | for example `OPENAI_API_KEY` with your own key |
2353	| `CDP_URL` | `http://127.0.0.1:9222`, browser 1 |
2354	| `CDP_URLS` | every browser's CDP URL in order, as a JSON array: `["http://127.0.0.1:9222"]` for one browser |
2355	| `BROWSER_COUNT` | how many browsers the sandbox started: `1` unless `agent.json` asks for more |
2356	| `DISPLAY` | `:1`, browser 1's screen; browser n is on `:n` |
2357	| `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY` (and lowercase) | `http://127.0.0.1:3128`, the only way out of the sandbox |
2358	| `NO_PROXY` | `localhost,127.0.0.1` (CDP stays local) |
2359	
2360	The platform sets no API key variables of its own, except the run-token placeholder for a provider the
2361	organizers pay for (above). `setup` runs first, with network (install your dependencies there) but without the
2362	run's variables or your team secrets, and nothing it starts survives into the run. The run itself reaches only our API and the challenge's websites,
2363	through that proxy; Chromium is already configured to use it. A scored run of RFQ has 20 minutes; a run that
2364	ends without an answer scores 0.

2366	## Browsers
2367	
2368	The sandbox starts one browser unless `agent.json` asks for more, up to four:
2369	
2370	```json
2371	{"setup": ["uv", "sync"], "run": ["uv", "run", "python", "agent.py"], "browsers": 3}
2372	```
2373	
2374	`browsers` is a whole number from 1 to 4; anything else rejects the package with
2375	`Invalid agent.json: browsers: must be a whole number from 1 to 4`. Browser n is its own headful Chromium with its
2376	own profile, on display `:n` (1280×800) with the Chrome DevTools Protocol on port 9221 + n (9222 to 9225), behind
2377	the same proxy as browser 1. All of them are ready before the clock starts. `CDP_URL` stays browser 1, `CDP_URLS` lists all of
2378	them in order, and `BROWSER_COUNT` says how many there are. With three:
2379	
2380	| Variable | Value |
2381	| --- | --- |
2382	| `CDP_URL` | `http://127.0.0.1:9222` |
2383	| `CDP_URLS` | `["http://127.0.0.1:9222","http://127.0.0.1:9223","http://127.0.0.1:9224"]` |
2384	| `BROWSER_COUNT` | `3` |
2385	
2386	**At most 4 browsers run at a time:** ask for up to 4 in `agent.json` (`"browsers"`), use tabs and browser contexts
2387	inside them freely, and don't start browsers of your own, headless ones included. The scored sandbox enforces it:
2388	any other browser the agent starts is stopped within seconds, and the run's logs say so with
2389	`[platform] stopped a browser the agent started: at most 4 run at a time; use the browsers from CDP_URLS`. Every
2390	browser then is one the platform can show and record: test runs show them side by side while they run, with a
2391	recording of each afterwards.
2392	
2393	On your own machine, developing with the scouting logins, `CDP_URLS` is not set and your agent starts its own
2394	browsers.

2400	# Building your agent
2401	
2402	Your agent system has to be agentic: a model decides where to go on the websites, finds the information and makes
2403	the decisions, at run time. How is up to you: drive the browser through the DOM, through pixels, or both; use one
2404	model or several, in parallel if you like; give the model tools and helpers for the browser, parsing, arithmetic and
2405	checks. The model chooses where to go, what to search for and which documents matter. Rejected in review: a fixed
2406	script that clicks through known pages with the model unused or only as a fallback, and a crawler that collects the
2407	websites and hands everything to the model at the end.
2408	
2409	## The browser
2410	
2411	In the sandbox a headful Chromium runs on the desktop (`DISPLAY=:1`, 1280×800) with CDP on
2412	`127.0.0.1:9222`.
2413	
2414	- **DOM agents:** attach with Playwright (`chromium.connect_over_cdp(CDP_URL)`) or any CDP client.
2415	- **Pixel agents:** take screenshots and send mouse and keyboard input to the desktop (`xdotool` and
2416	  ImageMagick's `import` are installed), for example to drive Claude's computer-use tool.
2417	- **Locally:** without `CDP_URL`, launch your own Chromium. The websites are the same: `eval "$(atira scout --env)"`
2418	  gives your agent the scouting logins in `CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS`, the way a run gets its logins.
2419	
2420	### Several browsers
2421	
2422	To work on several websites at once, ask for up to four browsers in `agent.json`:
2423	
2424	```json
2425	{"setup": ["npm", "ci"], "run": ["node", "agent.js"], "browsers": 2}
2426	```
2427	
2428	Each is its own Chromium on its own screen (browser n on `DISPLAY=:n`), and `CDP_URLS` lists their CDP URLs in
2429	order (`CDP_URL` stays the first). With Playwright:
2430	
2431	```javascript
2432	import { chromium } from "playwright"
2433	
2434	const sites = JSON.parse(process.env.CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS)
2435	const browsers = await Promise.all(JSON.parse(process.env.CDP_URLS).map((url) => chromium.connectOverCDP(url)))
2436	const pages = browsers.map((browser) => browser.contexts()[0].pages()[0])
2437	await Promise.all([pages[0].goto(sites[0].url), pages[1].goto(sites[1].url)])
2438	```
2439	
2440	At most 4 browsers run at a time. Use tabs (`context.newPage()`) and browser contexts (`browser.newContext()`)
2441	inside them as freely as you like, but don't start browsers of your own, headless ones included: the sandbox stops
2442	them and says so in the run's logs. A test run shows its browsers side by side while it runs and keeps a recording
2443	of each. Locally there is no `CDP_URLS`: on your machine your agent starts its own browsers.
2444	
2445	## Models
2446	
2447	The hosted models are free to use. Every run gets `QWEN_BASE_URL` and `QWEN_API_KEY` for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, an
2448	OpenAI-compatible chat model with tool calls and images; on your machine `atira scout --env` sets the same variables,
2449	pointed at `atira models proxy`. You can also bring your own key for any provider through the metering proxy;
2450	[how cost is measured](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#how-cost-is-measured) has the details. After quality you are ranked on cost × time, so a cheaper model or a faster run that gets the answer right moves you
2451	up.
2452	
2453	## What makes it hard, on purpose
2454	
2455	The websites are designed to trip agents up: cookie walls, flaky error pages that need a retry, expiring sessions
2456	that send you back to the login, documents inside iframes and ZIP files, popups that close themselves, paging and
2457	"load more" buttons, look-alike records, superseded versions shown first, a timezone that is not yours. Treat
2458	every page as adversarial and verify what you read.
2459	
2460	## Tips
2461	
2462	- Read the brief's rules carefully: they define the one correct answer.
2463	- Keep what the model reads small: page text without duplicated labels, only the parts you need.
2464	- Use prompt caching for your system prompt and tool definitions.
2465	- Re-read a page after every action that changes it; pages update asynchronously.
2466	- Drive four browsers in parallel, one per website (`"browsers": 4`, see [Several browsers](#several-browsers)):
2467	  reading the four sites at once speeds up each run and your iteration, at the cost of more complex code.
2468	- Validate your answer against `answer_schema` before sending it; a `400` costs only time.
2469	- Submit before the clock runs out: a scored run has 20 minutes (`expires_at` in the run). Every part of the answer
2470	  scores on its own, so have your agent submit its best answer about a minute before the end rather than keep
2471	  searching; a run that ends without an answer scores 0.
2472	- Develop against the public websites locally (`atira scout --env`), then test in the sandbox (`atira test-run`):
2473	  a test run shows the full score breakdown, so use it to find what your agent gets wrong.
2474	- Work the answer out from the websites: the final run, which weighs most for the winners, uses a private dataset that is similar, not the same. It has the same jobs (a tender portal, a supplier portal, an ERP and a webmail inbox), the same bid rules and the same answer format, but different software, with a different look, navigation and site names, other content and data, and the information split differently across them. Your agent has to handle it as it finds it.
2475	
2476	## Starter kit
2477	
2478	[`starter-kit/`](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/starter-kit.tar.gz) is a minimal Python skeleton, not an agent: it reads the run and
2479	submits an answer, attaches to the run's browsers over CDP with Playwright, and shows one call to each hosted model.
2480	Your agent goes in `solve()` in `agent.py`; out of the box it exits without an answer. Start from it or from scratch.

2486	# Fair play
2487	
2488	**Rules at a glance**
2489	
2490	You submit an agentic system: one agent or several. In the sandbox it does the whole job on its own: finds what it needs on the four websites, works out the bid and submits it. Nobody helps it during a run.
2491	
2492	**Not allowed**
2493	
2494	- **Hardcoding:** copying values from the websites into your package (prices, material numbers, totals, discounts, logins, TANs), including in prompts and notes, also as defaults or fallbacks. Using what the task brief tells every team, like the sales director's mailbox, is fine.
2495	- **Pre-solving:** working out the answer yourself, or having an AI assistant do it, and putting the result in your package. Exploring the sites with an assistant is fine.
2496	- **Scripts instead of agents:** a fixed click path, or a crawler that grabs everything for one model call. A model has to choose where to go, what to search for and what matters.
2497	- **Outside help during a run:** contacting anything besides our platform and the four websites, calling a model other than through our proxy (your own API keys work through it), running a model inside the sandbox, or starting your own browsers (use the up to 4 provided). Setup may install dependencies.
2498	
2499	**How it's checked:** an AI reviewer reads every submitted package before its scored run. Unclear cases are flagged and stay off the leaderboard until an organizer has looked. The final runs on websites and data your system hasn't seen.
2500	
2501	The details follow.
2502	
2503	## Allowed
2504	
2505	- Any agent design; the free hosted models, or any provider and model with your own key, through the proxy; any
2506	  amount of tokens.
2507	  The proxy forwards your calls unchanged and measures them: reported usage is metered at the published model
2508	  prices, and an upstream-reported USD cost takes precedence. See [the run contract](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#llm-calls)
2509	  for SDK configuration.
2510	- Keeping your model key as a [team secret](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#team-secrets) rather than in your package.
2511	- Your own code, prompts and tools; open-source libraries installed during setup.
2512	- Using what you learned with the scouting logins and in test runs about how the websites work.
2513	- Up to 4 browsers at a time: ask for them with `"browsers"` in `agent.json` and use as many tabs and browser
2514	  contexts inside them as you like.
2515	
2516	## Not allowed
2517	
2518	- Hardcoding values copied from the public scenario or its websites into code, config, prompts or notes, including defaults and fallbacks: tender references, material numbers, prices, totals, discounts, logins and TANs. Facts the task brief states for every scenario, such as the sales director's mailbox, are
2519	  rules you may use.
2520	- A scripted solution. Your agent system must be agentic: a model decides where to go on the websites, finds the
2521	  information and makes the decisions. Code can help it (browser control, parsing, arithmetic, checks, reading a
2522	  page or document the model chose, paging through results it asked for), and several agents and browsers may work
2523	  in parallel. Rejected: a fixed script that clicks through known pages with the model unused or only as a fallback,
2524	  and a crawler that collects the websites and hands everything to the model at the end.
2525	- Bundling or running a local model, or reaching any model other than through the proxy.
2526	- Contacting hosts other than the API and the challenge's websites, or trying to get data out of the sandbox.
2527	- Starting browsers of your own in the sandbox, headless ones included. At most 4 browsers run at a time: ask for up
2528	  to 4 in `agent.json` (`"browsers"`), use tabs and browser contexts inside them freely, and don't start others.
2529	  On your own machine (developing with the scouting logins) your agent starts its own browsers; that is up to you.
2530	- Attacking the platform, the websites, the sandbox or other teams; sharing scored-run data.
2531	
2532	## How it is checked
2533	
2534	- **Package review before any scored run:** an AI code reviewer, a coding agent that reads your whole package in an
2535	  isolated VM. Outcomes: passed, flagged or rejected (no runs). A flagged package still runs and scores, but its
2536	  result stays off the public leaderboard and the activity feed until an organizer passes it; your team sees it
2537	  marked "flagged: waiting for an organizer". Notes and docs addressed to the reviewer are not evidence of compliance
2538	  and do not count against you on their own. Instructions trying to steer the reviewer's verdict do.
2539	  The reviewer's reasons stay with the organizers: your team reads "Flagged by the reviewing agent" or "Rejected by
2540	  the reviewing agent". Someone from Atira looks at flagged packages shortly and unflags a misdetection; if you think
2541	  a reject is one, contact the Atira team.
2542	- **The organizers decide flagged packages, and can look at any submission:** they pass it, add an internal note
2543	  (this changes nothing you or the leaderboard see) or disqualify it. A disqualified submission and its runs read
2544	  "disqualified": it leaves the leaderboard and the final run, its runs still going stop, and your team page shows the
2545	  organizers' reason.
2546	- **Hardcoded values:** the reviewer rejects copied scenario values in code or config, even in defaults or fallbacks.
2547	- **The final run** uses a private dataset that is similar, not the same. It has the same jobs (a tender portal, a
2548	  supplier portal, an ERP and a webmail inbox), the same bid rules and the same answer format, but different software,
2549	  with a different look, navigation and site names, other content and data, and the information split differently
2550	  across them. Your agent has to handle it as it finds it. That run weighs most when we pick the
2551	  winners, so build a system that works the answer out from the websites, not one tuned to the public scenario.
2552	- **The sandbox** reaches only our API and the websites, so every model call passes the proxy and is measured.
2553	  Your team secrets reach only the timed run step and are redacted from its logs.
2554	- **Website logins** exist only for a live run and stop working when it ends.
2555	- **Browsers:** the sandbox stops any browser your agent starts beyond the ones it asked for and notes it in the
2556	  run's logs: `[platform] stopped a browser the agent started`.
2557	- **Everything measured** (tokens, cost, time, the answer) is recorded by the platform, never reported by you.
2558	
2559	Breaking these rules gets the submission rejected before it runs, or removed later; repeated or deliberate attempts
2560	get the team disqualified.
2561	
2562	## Flagged results
2563	
2564	A flagged result stays off the public leaderboard until an organizer passes it. **Show flagged** on the leaderboard
2565	lists flagged results, without a rank.

2571	# Submitting
2572	
2573	> In this document, `$API` is https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai (the CLI and API guide call it `$ATIRA_API`).
2574	
2575	You submit your agent system as a gzipped tarball. We review it, run it once in the sandbox on the public dataset
2576	and score it. That run determines its rank on the leaderboard. When the hackathon ends, your latest submission that
2577	passed review runs once more, on a private dataset, in the [final run](#what-happens-next), which weighs most when we pick the winners.
2578	
2579	## Package layout
2580	
2581	```
2582	agent.json          {"setup": ["uv", "sync"], "run": ["uv", "run", "python", "agent.py"], "models": ["qwen"]}
2583	pyproject.toml      (or package.json, requirements.txt, ...)
2584	agent.py            your code
2585	```
2586	
2587	- `agent.json` at the root: `setup` (optional) and `run`, each an argv array. Both run in the package directory.
2588	  `browsers` (optional, 1 to 4, default 1) is how many browsers the sandbox starts for the run; see
2589	  [the run contract](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#browsers). `models` (optional) lists the hosted models your agent system calls,
2590	  by provider id, all of them by default: the run's clock waits for those to warm up, and `[]` starts it right after
2591	  setup; see [the run contract](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#scored-run).
2592	- At most 20 MB compressed; regular files only.
2593	- No secrets: the run gets everything it needs from the environment.
2594	
2595	## Upload
2596	
2597	```
2598	tar czf agent.tar.gz -C my-agent .
2599	curl --data-binary @agent.tar.gz \
2600	  -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN" -H "content-type: application/gzip" \
2601	  $API/v1/challenges/rfq/submissions
2602	```
2603	
2604	The response (`202`) has your submission's id. Review is still pending and no runs exist yet: follow it with
2605	`GET $API/v1/challenges/rfq/submissions` for the review result and run ids, or watch the leaderboard.
2606	
2607	`$ATIRA_TOKEN` is your personal token: `atira login` signs the [CLI](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/cli.md) in through the browser, and
2608	`atira token` prints the token (or sign in with plain curl, as the [API guide](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/api.md#signing-in) shows).
2609	
2610	Or let the CLI pack, check and upload the folder: `atira submit my-agent` (and `atira test-run my-agent` for a
2611	test run). It leaves out `.git`, `node_modules` and what `.gitignore` excludes. In a terminal, `submit` then opens
2612	your team page, which shows the review and links each scored run as it starts, and `test-run` opens the run page.
2613	
2614	## Test it in the sandbox first
2615	
2616	Upload the same tarball as a test run ("Test runs" on your team page, or
2617	`POST $API/v1/challenges/rfq/rehearsals` with the same headers). It runs once in the scored-run sandbox against
2618	the public scenario `public-1`, scored with the points for each part of the answer. Its live view shows the
2619	browser (a frame about every 1.5 s, or the live screen where available), the phases, every model call,
2620	and your logs as the agent prints them. Afterwards the recorded video stays available to
2621	your team. Up to 7 test runs at a time per team. `atira test-run my-agent` uploads it, starts the run
2622	and opens it live; `atira cancel` (or Cancel run on the run page) stops a run that has not finished, and frees its
2623	test-run slot at once.
2624	
2625	## Linking your GitHub repository
2626	
2627	The organizers ask each team to link the GitHub repository it builds its agent in, so they can review the
2628	code, for example to compare a winning submission with its source. On your team page, the captain chooses
2629	Connect a GitHub repository, installs the organizers' GitHub App on the account that owns the repository
2630	(granting it only that repository is enough), and picks the repository. Every member sees the linked repository,
2631	who linked it and when; the captain can switch or unlink it at any time.
2632	
2633	The app only reads the contents of the repositories you grant it; it cannot push, open issues or change
2634	settings. Linking does not change how you submit: scored submissions and test runs are still the tarballs
2635	described above. To withdraw access completely, unlink the repository and uninstall the app in your GitHub
2636	settings.
2637	
2638	## Watching your submission
2639	
2640	Each scored run has a live view with its phase, timer, model calls, tokens and cost. On the public dataset it also
2641	shows your team the browser (frames, and the live screen where available), the logs and errors
2642	unredacted and the scenario id, and the recording afterwards. The final run on the private dataset shows its
2643	screen, frames and recordings to the organizers only; your team reads its logs and errors with private values
2644	masked as `[private]`.
2645	
2646	## Resubmitting
2647	
2648	Submit as often as you like, one at a time: while a submission is still in review or has unfinished runs, the
2649	next upload is refused with `429`. Your **best complete** submission holds your place on the leaderboard; your
2650	**latest** one that passed review goes into the final run. Your other submissions stay in your history at
2651	`$API/team`. Cancelling a submission's scored run ends that submission: it never completes, the leaderboard ignores it, and you
2652	can submit again.
2653	
2654	## What happens next
2655	
2656	1. **Review:** passed, flagged or rejected (no runs). A flagged submission still runs and scores, but its result
2657	   stays off the public leaderboard and the activity feed until an organizer passes it; your team sees it marked
2658	   "flagged: waiting for an organizer". Your team sees the outcome, not the reviewer's reasons. The organizers can
2659	   still pass or disqualify a submission later; a disqualified one reads "disqualified", leaves the leaderboard and
2660	   the final run, and your team page gives the organizers' reason.
2661	2. **Scored run:** one run in a fresh sandbox on the public dataset, setup first (up to 5 minutes, not counted),
2662	   then your run command (timed).
2663	3. **Ranking:** once the run has finished and review is passed, your submission appears on the leaderboard with its quality, cost and
2664	   time; ineligible answers rank after every eligible one.
2665	4. **Final run:** when the hackathon ends, the organizers run every team's latest submission that passed review
2666	   (organizers resolve outstanding reviewer flags before the final run starts; rejected and disqualified ones don't count) once by default (or best of three if you opt in before the final run starts) on a private dataset that is similar, not the same. It has the same jobs (a tender portal, a supplier portal, an ERP and a webmail inbox), the same bid rules and the same answer format, but different software, with a different look, navigation and site names, other content and data, and the information split differently across them. Your agent has to handle it as it finds it. It is the latest one, not the best one.
2667	   That run weighs most when we pick the winners ([Winners](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/scoring.md#winners)), so build a system that works the answer out from the websites, not one tuned to
2668	   the public scenario. Its results stay with the organizers until they publish them; then the leaderboard shows
2669	   the final results, tagged "Private dataset · final", and the public-dataset board stays at
2670	   `$API/challenges/rfq/leaderboard?dataset=public`.
2671

2674	The final runs your latest passed submission once, or up to three times if you opt in to **Best of 3** on your team
2675	page before the final starts (`atira final --best-of 3`). Your best attempt counts. Details:
2676	[Answers and scoring](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/scoring.md#final-private-evaluation-one-attempt-or-best-of-three).

2703	## FAQ
2704	
2705	**Which models can I use?** The hosted models are free, and the starter kit shows how to call them. Or bring your own key for
2706	any provider (Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Google, Groq, Mistral, DeepSeek, xAI, Together, Fireworks, or others the
2707	organizers add) and send its calls through the metering proxy. `GET /v1/runs/current` lists the proxy base URLs. Models must have a published
2708	price (a model too new for the platform's list counts at the price OpenRouter lists for it; OpenRouter reports its own)
2709	and satisfy any organizer model allowlist. See
2710	[the run contract](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#llm-calls) for SDK setup.
2711	
2712	**Where do I keep my model key?** As a [team secret](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#team-secrets): the team page's Secrets list
2713	injects it into your agent's run step in test and scored runs, redacted from logs. Don't put keys in your
2714	package; we store packages and the review agent reads them.
2715	
2716	**Why does my model call get a 401?** "Add your OpenAI API key to the request" means no provider key arrived: set
2717	`OPENAI_API_KEY` (in test and scored runs, as a [team secret](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#team-secrets)). A 401 from the
2718	provider itself means the key is wrong. Check that `OPENAI_BASE_URL` points at the run's proxy
2719	(`$LLM_PROXY_URL/openai/v1`, already set in test and scored runs); the same holds for any OpenAI-compatible provider.
2720	
2721	**How do my teammates and I sign in from a terminal?** Each person runs `atira login` on their own computer
2722	and approves it in the browser. Every device gets its own token; there is no shared team key to pass around.
2723	Without a browser on the machine, `atira login --device` prints a link and a code to approve elsewhere.
2724	
2725	**I lost a laptop, or a token leaked.** Revoke that device's token on your team page under Signed-in devices
2726	(`atira logout` revokes the one on the computer you are at). Leaving or being removed from a team ends your
2727	tokens' access to it at once.
2728	
2729	**My invite link says it is for someone else.** Invites are for one GitHub account. Sign in with the account
2730	the captain invited, or ask the captain to invite your GitHub username.
2731	
2732	**Does it cost me anything?** We charge nothing, and the models the platform hosts are free and never charged. If
2733	you bring your own key for another provider, that provider bills your key. The proxy measures every call and
2734	ranks you on its cost at the published prices; hosted calls count at simulated API prices.
2735	
2736	**How can I try my agent?** Develop locally against the public websites (`atira scout --env` exports the
2737	scouting logins), then test in the sandbox (`atira test-run ./my-agent`). A test run runs on `public-1`, the public
2738	RFQ scenario, and returns your score with the points for each part of the answer. With the scouting logins nothing
2739	counts: a bid entered on the tender portal is acknowledged without counting.
2740	
2741	**Is the public scenario's answer published?** No. The correct answer isn't published; your system has to work it
2742	out from the websites. Score breakdowns show the points for each part of the answer, never the expected values.
2743	
2744	**Which submission counts?** Your best submission holds your place on the leaderboard, which ranks scored runs on
2745	the public dataset. Your latest one that passed review (not your best one) goes into the final run: when the
2746	hackathon ends, the organizers run it once by default (or best of three if you opt in before the final run starts) on a private dataset that is similar, not the same. It has the same jobs (a tender portal, a supplier portal, an ERP and a webmail inbox), the same bid rules and the same answer format, but different software, with a different look, navigation and site names, other content and data, and the information split differently across them. Your agent has to handle it as it finds it.
2747	That run weighs most when we pick the winners, ahead of your public score and the elegance of your system, so
2748	build an agent that works the answer out from the websites, not one tuned to the public scenario. See
2749	[Winners](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/scoring.md#winners).
2750	
2751	**Why did my answer get a 400?** It does not match `answer_schema`. The response lists the issues; the run is
2752	still open, so fix it and send it again.
2753	
2754	**Can I run my agent outside the sandbox?** While you develop, yes, anywhere, with the scouting logins. Test runs
2755	and scored runs always run in our sandbox.
2756	
2757	**Why is my run still queued?** Runs share the sandboxes in a fair order: scored runs first, then teams take turns,
2758	the team with the fewest runs in flight first. Your team runs up to 7 test runs at a time and can have up to 3
2759	waiting; the next waits while other teams' runs start. The run page says how many runs are ahead of yours, and
2760	`atira test-run --follow` prints it. See [the run queue](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/api.md#the-run-queue).
2761	
2762	**How do I stop a run?** `atira cancel <run>`, or Cancel run on its run page. The sandbox is removed, the run fails
2763	with "Cancelled by @you", and you can start the next test run at once. A cancelled scored run ends its
2764	submission: the leaderboard ignores it, and you can submit again.
2765	
2766	**Why do my requests get a 403 "Error 1010"?** The edge in front of our hosts refuses some default HTTP
2767	clients, such as Python's `urllib`. Send your own `User-Agent` header (the starter kit does).
2768	
2769	**Python says `CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED` on my Mac.** Python from python.org ships without CA certificates.
2770	Run `Install Certificates.command` from its folder in Applications, or set `SSL_CERT_FILE=/etc/ssl/cert.pem`.
2771	
2772	**What can my agent reach during a scored run?** Our API (including the model proxy) and the challenge's
2773	websites, nothing else. The `HTTP(S)_PROXY` variables in the run's environment route there; Python's
2774	`urllib`, `requests`, `httpx`, the Anthropic SDK and Node's `fetch` pick them up automatically. Chromium is
2775	already configured. Setup (`uv sync`, `npm ci`, …) has network, but nothing it starts survives into the
2776	run.

2795	# API guide
2796	
2797	The platform's HTTP API, step by step, with curl examples for everything a team or its agent does. The complete
2798	reference, with every endpoint, request body, response and error, is `/openapi.json` on the platform.
2799	
2800	## Basics
2801	
2802	```sh
2803	export ATIRA_API=https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai
2804	export ATIRA_TOKEN=$(atira token)   # your personal token, after `atira login` (or sign in with curl, below)
2805	```
2806	
2807	- **Credentials** go in the `x-api-key` header: your personal token (`atp_...`) for your team's endpoints, a run
2808	  token (`rt_...`) for the run's own endpoints. `Authorization: Bearer` works too.
2809	- **Personal tokens** belong to one person and one device. A token acts as you on the team you are in at the
2810	  time of the request, so leaving or being removed from the team ends its access at once. It lasts 90 days; revoke
2811	  it on your team page under Signed-in devices, with `atira logout`, or with the API (below).
2812	- **Without GitHub sign-in**, a team registers with `POST /v1/teams` and gets a team key (`tk_...`) once; it goes
2813	  where the personal token goes.
2814	- **User agent:** send one of your own. The edge refuses some default clients, such as Python's `urllib`.
2815	- **Errors** are JSON: `{"type": "error", "error": {"type": "not_found_error", "message": "run not found"}}`.
2816	
2817	| Status | Error type | Meaning |
2818	| --- | --- | --- |
2819	| 400 | `invalid_request_error` | The body, a parameter or the package is invalid. The message says what. |
2820	| 401 | `authentication_error` | The token is missing, unknown, revoked or expired, or its run has ended. |
2821	| 403 | `permission_error` | Valid, but not allowed: for example, only the captain may, or your account is in no team. |
2822	| 404 | `not_found_error` | Not found, or not yours. |
2823	| 409 | `conflict_error` | Conflicts with the current state, for example an answer sent to the API when the challenge takes it on a website. |
2824	| 413 | `invalid_request_error` | The body is over its limit. |
2825	| 429 | `rate_limit_error` | Busy: one submission in evaluation at a time, at most 3 test runs waiting. Try again later. |
2826	
2827	## Signing in
2828	
2829	`atira login` signs the [CLI](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/cli.md) in through the browser: approve once, and it stores a personal token for
2830	this device. Without a browser on the machine, `atira login --device` prints a link and a code instead. Plain
2831	curl does the same with the device flow.
2832	
2833	### With curl: the device flow
2834	
2835	1. Ask for a code. The label names the device on your team page.
2836	
2837	   ```sh
2838	   device=$(curl -s -X POST "$ATIRA_API/v1/cli/device" \
2839	     -H "content-type: application/json" -d '{"label": "my-laptop"}')
2840	   printf '%s\n' "$device"
2841	   ```
2842	
2843	   ```json
2844	   {"device_code": "atd_...", "user_code": "BCDF-GHJK",
2845	    "verification_url": "https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/cli/device?code=BCDF-GHJK",
2846	    "expires_in": 600, "interval": 5}
2847	   ```
2848	
2849	2. Open `verification_url` in a browser (sign in with GitHub there if asked), check that the code matches, and
2850	   choose Approve. A coding agent prints the link for its person to open.
2851	
2852	3. Poll for the token, no faster than every `interval` seconds:
2853	
2854	   ```sh
2855	   DEVICE_CODE=$(printf '%s' "$device" | jq -r .device_code)
2856	   interval=$(printf '%s' "$device" | jq .interval)
2857	   while :; do
2858	     sleep "$interval"
2859	     reply=$(curl -s -X POST "$ATIRA_API/v1/cli/token" \
2860	       -H "content-type: application/json" -d "{\"device_code\": \"$DEVICE_CODE\"}")
2861	     case $(printf '%s' "$reply" | jq -r '.error.type // "signed-in"') in
2862	       signed-in) export ATIRA_TOKEN=$(printf '%s' "$reply" | jq -r .token); break ;;
2863	       authorization_pending) ;;
2864	       slow_down) interval=$(printf '%s' "$reply" | jq .interval) ;;
2865	       rate_limit_error) interval=$((interval + 5)) ;;
2866	       *) printf '%s\n' "$reply" | jq -r .error.message; break ;;
2867	     esac
2868	   done
2869	   ```
2870	
2871	| Answer | Meaning |
2872	| --- | --- |
2873	| `200` | Approved: `{"token", "token_id", "label", "expires_at", "user"}`. The token is shown this once. |
2874	| `400` `authorization_pending` | Not approved yet. Poll again after `interval` seconds. |
2875	| `400` `slow_down` | Polled too soon. Wait 5 seconds longer from now on; the body's `interval` is the new pace. |
2876	| `400` `access_denied` | Cancelled in the browser. |
2877	| `400` `expired_token` | Not approved within 10 minutes. Start again. |
2878	| `400` `invalid_grant` | An unknown code, or one that was already used. |
2879	| `429` `rate_limit_error` | Too many sign-in requests from this network. Wait 5 seconds longer and poll again. |
2880	
2881	Then:
2882	
2883	```sh
2884	curl "$ATIRA_API/v1/me" -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN"          # you, your team, this token's expiry
2885	curl "$ATIRA_API/v1/me/tokens" -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN"   # your signed-in devices
2886	curl -X DELETE "$ATIRA_API/v1/me/tokens/$TOKEN_ID" -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN"   # revoke one of them
2887	curl -X DELETE "$ATIRA_API/v1/cli/token" -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN"             # revoke this one
2888	```
2889	
2890	### The browser flow
2891	
2892	`atira login` listens on `127.0.0.1` at a random port and opens
2893	`$ATIRA_API/cli/authorize?port=...&state=...&code_challenge=...&label=...` (PKCE with SHA-256). After you approve,
2894	the browser goes to `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback?code=...&state=...`; the CLI checks `state` and exchanges
2895	`{"code", "code_verifier"}` at `POST /v1/cli/token` for the same response as above. A code works once and expires
2896	after 5 minutes, and the platform only ever sends the browser back to a port on `127.0.0.1`. Both flows are rate
2897	limited like signing in.

2912	Develop your agent on your own machine against the public websites, then test it in the sandbox. The scouting

2920	website's `siteId`, `url` and `credentials`: the JSON a run gets as `CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS`), `submission`, `brief`,
2921	`answer_schema` and a `note`: the run's own fields from `/v1/runs/current`, minus anything tied to a run token. Before
2922	the organizers publish logins it answers `404`. These are demo logins without a run token: your agent calls its model
2923	with your own key, and nothing done with them counts. A bid entered on the tender portal is acknowledged without
2924	counting. `atira scout --env` prints the logins as shell exports and, where the organizers host models, their

2927	## The current run
2928	
2929	With the run token, inside the sandbox (`$CHALLENGE_API_URL` and `$CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN`):
2930	
2931	```sh
2932	export ATIRA_API=$CHALLENGE_API_URL RUN_TOKEN=$CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN
2933	curl "$ATIRA_API/v1/runs/current" -H "x-api-key: $RUN_TOKEN"
2934	```
2935	
2936	Keep the token secret: it is the run's identity, its key to the model proxy, and the only way to hand in its
2937	answer.
2938	
2939	It returns `brief` (the task in Markdown, with the rules), `access` (each website's `siteId`, `url` and
2940	`credentials`), `submission` (where the answer goes), `answer_schema`, `started_at`, `expires_at`,
2941	`spent_micro_usd`, `llm_proxy_url` and `llm_providers`.
2942	
2943	When `submission.kind` is `api`, post the answer as JSON:
2944	
2945	```sh
2946	curl -X POST "$ATIRA_API/v1/runs/current/answer" \
2947	  -H "x-api-key: $RUN_TOKEN" -H "content-type: application/json" -d @answer.json
2948	```

2950	- `400` with `{"issues": [{"path", "message"}]}`: the answer does not match the schema. Nothing is recorded and
2951	  the clock keeps running; fix it and send it again.
2952	- `202`: accepted and final. The run ends; a test run's response carries `quality`, `eligible` and the
2953	  `breakdown`. The agent has 10 seconds to exit before the platform stops it.
2954	
2955	When `submission.kind` is `site` (RFQ), the answer goes through that website instead, and this endpoint answers
2956	`409`.
2957	
2958	Model calls go through `$LLM_PROXY_URL/<provider>/...` (the run token is in the path, your own provider key in its usual header); the
2959	[run contract](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#llm-calls) has the settings for each SDK.

2961	## Test runs
2962	
2963	A test run uploads your package and runs it once in the scored-run sandbox on the public scenario, with live
2964	browser frames, logs and a recording.
2965	
2966	```sh
2967	tar czf agent.tar.gz -C my-agent .
2968	curl --data-binary @agent.tar.gz \
2969	  -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN" -H "content-type: application/gzip" \
2970	  "$ATIRA_API/v1/challenges/rfq/rehearsals"
2971	```
2972	
2973	`202` returns `{"rehearsal_id", "run_id", "package"}`, with `package` the upload's `{"sha256", "files", "label"}`:
2974	the SHA-256 of the gzip, its number of files, and the `?label=` you gave it (at most 100 printable characters, for
2975	example a git commit; null without one). Submissions take `?label=` too, and every run lists the `package` it ran. The
2976	run page `$ATIRA_API/runs/$RUN_ID` shows it live, with the score and
2977	its full breakdown once it is done. A package that can't be read (no `agent.json`, over the size limits) is refused with `400`; a test run beyond
2978	your team's queued ones with `429`. `atira test-run ./my-agent` does the same and opens
2979	the run page.
2980	
2981	### The run queue
2982	
2983	Test and scored runs wait in one queue for the sandboxes and start in a fair order:
2984	
2985	- Scored runs start before test runs.
2986	- Within each kind, teams take turns: the team with the fewest runs in flight goes next, then the oldest waiting run.
2987	  A team with five waiting runs takes one turn while every other team takes theirs.
2988	- Your team runs up to 7 test runs at a time; the next one waits while other teams' runs start. Up to 3 of your
2989	  test runs can wait; one more is refused with `429` ("You already have 3 test runs queued; wait for one to start.").
2990	  Cancelling a waiting test run frees its place at once.
2991	- Package reviews have slots of their own, so a burst of submissions never holds back runs.
2992	
2993	These are the defaults; the organizers may adjust the numbers during the event. While a run waits,
2994	`GET /v1/runs/{run_id}` and its feed carry `queue_position` (1 starts next), `runs_ahead`, a rough
2995	`estimated_start_s` and `team_limit_reached` (it waits for one of your team's running test runs to end); once it has started they are
2996	`null` (and `false`). The run page shows "Queued: 3 runs ahead of yours", and `atira test-run --follow` and
2997	`atira submit --follow` print it whenever it changes.
2998

3007	```
3008	
3009	`202` returns `{"submission_id", "review_status": "pending", "findings": [], "run_ids": []}`. The package must be a
3010	gzipped tarball with `agent.json` at its root, regular files only, at most 20 MB compressed (2,000 files, 5 MB per
3011	file, 20 MB in total). While a submission is in review or running, the next one is refused with `429`.
3012	
3013	```sh
3014	curl "$ATIRA_API/v1/challenges/rfq/submissions" -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN"
3015	curl "$ATIRA_API/v1/teams/me/submissions/$SUBMISSION_ID" -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN"
3016	```
3017	
3018	A submission's `status` is `in_review`, `rejected`, `in_evaluation`, `complete` or `failed`;
3019	`review_status` is `pending`, `passed`, `awaiting_organizer_review`, `rejected` or `disqualified`.
3020	A flagged submission still runs and scores; your team sees its result, but the public leaderboard and activity feed
3021	show it only once an organizer passes it.
3022	`findings` never holds the reviewer's reasons: a reviewer flag or reject reads as one line, and an organizer's
3023	verdict as a sentence with its note. Its `dataset` (`"public"` or `"private"`) is the
3024	dataset its scored runs use, and each run in its summary carries `dataset` and, on the public dataset only,
3025	`scenario_id`.

3027	### Your packages
3028	
3029	```sh
3030	curl -OJ "$ATIRA_API/v1/runs/$RUN_ID/package" -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN"                     # a run's .tar.gz
3031	curl -OJ "$ATIRA_API/v1/teams/me/submissions/$SUBMISSION_ID/package" -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN" # a submission's
3032	curl "$ATIRA_API/v1/runs/$RUN_ID/package/files" -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN"                   # what it holds
3033	```
3034	
3035	Your team downloads the package each of its test runs, scored runs and submissions used: the gzipped tarball it
3036	uploaded, byte for byte, named `<team>-<id>.tar.gz`, with its SHA-256 in `X-Atira-SHA256`. A scored run's package is
3037	its submission's, which the final evaluation's copies of that submission share. `/package/files` lists the same
3038	package without the contents: `{"id", "sha256", "label", "bytes", "agent_json", "files": [{"path", "bytes"}]}`.
3039	Only your own: another team's run or submission is `404`.
3040	Your team page links each submission's and test run's package, and the run page links the run's for your team's
3041	members. `atira package <id> --out <dir>` and the MCP tool `run_package` do the same.

3043	## Runs
3044	
3045	```sh
3046	curl "$ATIRA_API/v1/runs" -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN"               # your runs, newest first
3047	curl "$ATIRA_API/v1/runs/$RUN_ID" -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN"       # one run, with its score
3048	curl "$ATIRA_API/v1/runs/$RUN_ID/feed" -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN"  # live: phase, status, calls, cost
3049	```
3050	
3051	A run's `phase` moves through `queued`, `provisioning`, `setup`, `running`, `scoring` and `done`; its `status`
3052	ends as `scored` or `submitted` (an answer was scored), `failed` or `timed_out`. Each run carries `dataset`:
3053	`"public"` for test runs and scored runs during the hackathon, `"private"` for the final run. On a private dataset,
3054	`scenario_id` is left out and `error` and `answer` are `null`: they stay with the organizers.
3055	
3056	A failed run says why in `failure_class`: `platform` (the platform failed, not your agent system: a sandbox fault, a
3057	lost connection, our own timeout, or a hosted model down for most of the run), `agent_exit` (setup or the run exited
3058	non-zero), `timeout`, `cancelled`, `no_answer` (it exited 0 without an answer) or `answer_rejected` (every answer it
3059	sent was invalid); `null` while it runs and once it succeeded. A `platform` failure has `counts: false`: it counts
3060	toward neither the ranking nor any limit, and its `error` reads "The platform failed, not your agent system. This
3061	run doesn't count; start it again." A scored run is queued again once by itself, as the run named in `retry_run_id`
3062	(whose `retry_of` names this one), and its `error` ends "it was started again automatically." instead.
3063	
3064	### Cancelling a run
3065	
3066	```sh
3067	curl -X POST "$ATIRA_API/v1/runs/$RUN_ID/cancel" -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN"
3068	```
3069	
3070	Your team cancels its own test runs and scored runs that have not finished (organizers can cancel any run). The run
3071	stops at once: its execution is aborted, its sandbox removed, its recording stopped and its live links revoked. It
3072	ends as `failed` with the error `Cancelled by @you` and `finished_at` set, and your team can start the next test run
3073	straight away. A queued run is cancelled before it starts. A cancelled scored run leaves its submission not
3074	complete: the leaderboard ignores that submission and you can submit again. `200` returns `{"run_id", "status": "failed", "error",
3075	"finished_at"}`; `404` means no such run of yours, `409` that it has already finished. In a browser session, send
3076	the `x-atira-csrf` header as for every write.
3077	
3078	### Logs
3079	
3080	Test runs and scored runs keep their output. Read it from a cursor: each page holds up to 128 chunks and the cursor
3081	to continue from.
3082	
3083	```sh
3084	cursor=0
3085	while :; do
3086	  page=$(curl -s "$ATIRA_API/v1/runs/$RUN_ID/logs?after=$cursor" -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN")
3087	  printf '%s' "$page" | jq -j '.chunks[].text'
3088	  next=$(printf '%s' "$page" | jq .cursor)
3089	  [ "$next" = "$cursor" ] && break
3090	  cursor=$next
3091	done
3092	```
3093	
3094	While the run is live, keep polling with a pause until `feed` reports `phase` `done` and its `log_cursor` is no
3095	newer than yours. Or follow them as they arrive, as server-sent events:
3096	
3097	```sh
3098	curl -N "$ATIRA_API/v1/runs/$RUN_ID/logs/stream?after=$cursor" -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN"
3099	```
3100	
3101	Each event is one chunk: `id` is its cursor and `data` is `{"at", "stream", "text"}`. Reconnect with
3102	`Last-Event-ID` (an `EventSource` does this by itself) or `?after=` to resume. A comment line (`: heartbeat`) comes
3103	every 15 seconds; once the run has finished and everything is sent, an `end` event closes the stream, and connecting
3104	again answers `204`. All of it at once, as JSON lines:
3105	
3106	```sh
3107	curl -o logs.jsonl "$ATIRA_API/v1/runs/$RUN_ID/logs.jsonl" -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN"
3108	```
3109	
3110	To look at one stretch of a run, query its lines by time and content. Times are on the run's clock, as the run page
3111	shows them: `mm:ss`, `h:mm:ss`, `3m20s` or seconds from the run's start (a minus is before it), or an ISO 8601 time.
3112	
3113	```sh
3114	curl -G "$ATIRA_API/v1/runs/$RUN_ID/logs/query" -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN" \
3115	  --data-urlencode from=02:10 --data-urlencode to=02:40 --data-urlencode stream=stdout,stderr \
3116	  --data-urlencode 'grep=error|timeout'
3117	```
3118	
3119	It answers `lines` (each with `t`, its milliseconds from the start, `clock` as `mm:ss.s`, `at`, `stream` and `text`),
3120	`matched` and `next`: up to `limit` lines (200 by default, at most 1,000), and `next` to pass as `after` while more
3121	match. `grep` is case-insensitive text; `a|b` matches either. The `input` stream holds the clicks, scrolls and typing
3122	the platform recorded in each browser, one line per action (`browser 1: click at 640,412`). Typed text is shown, with
3123	keys, tokens, your run's secrets and password or one-time-code fields masked. Lines come in time order across
3124	streams. A click, drag or drop gives its point on the browser's 1280×800 display (Chrome's bar included) and, when
3125	the platform knew the page's geometry, the same point in the page's viewport with the viewport's size:
3126	`browser 1: click at 200,685 (viewport 200,542 of 1279x656)`. Frames and recordings show the viewport alone, so that
3127	point lands on a frame at 200/1279 of its width and 542/656 of its height.
3128	
3129	`GET /v1/runs/$RUN_ID/llm-calls` lists the run's model calls in order (`at`, `provider`, `model`, `status`, tokens,
3130	`cost_micro_usd`, `latency_ms`, and `queue_ms`, how long a call to a hosted model waited for a GPU), up to `limit`
3131	(2,000 by default) with `next` to pass as `after`. `GET /v1/runs/$RUN_ID/screen-activity` gives, per browser, the
3132	spans during which its screen kept changing: a gap between spans is a time the screen sat still.
3133	
3134	Runs on the public dataset (test runs and scored runs during the hackathon) keep their logs unredacted. On a
3135	private dataset (the final run), your logs and the feed's `error` have private values masked as `[private]`.
3136	
3137	### Frames and recordings
3138	
3139	```sh
3140	curl -o frame.jpg "$ATIRA_API/v1/runs/$RUN_ID/frame" -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN"   # the latest frame
3141	curl -o run.webm "$ATIRA_API/v1/runs/$RUN_ID/video" -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN"    # the recording
3142	curl -X POST "$ATIRA_API/v1/runs/$RUN_ID/video/share" -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN"  # a link anyone can watch
3143	curl -X DELETE "$ATIRA_API/v1/runs/$RUN_ID/video/share" -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN"
3144	```
3145	
3146	A browser's screen at any time of a finished run, cut from its recording as a PNG:
3147	
3148	```sh
3149	curl -o at-0213.png "$ATIRA_API/v1/runs/$RUN_ID/frame?t=02:13&browser=1" -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN"
3150	```
3151	
3152	`t` takes the same times as the log query, to the nearest quarter second; outside the recording you get its first or
3153	last frame. `X-Run-Clock` names the frame's time. Whoever may watch the recording may ask for its frames. The
3154	platform cuts them with ffmpeg, two at a time: `429` means it is busy (retry after `Retry-After`), and `503` with
3155	error type `frames_unavailable` means it can't right now, so cut the frame yourself from `video/source` (`ffmpeg -ss
3156	133 -i "<url>" -frames:v 1 frame.png`; `atira mcp` does this for you when ffmpeg is installed).
3157	
3158	`frame` without `t` answers `204` until there is a frame, and `304` for an unchanged one sent with `If-None-Match`. `video` serves
3159	byte ranges. `video/source` tells a player where to read the recording: a presigned URL straight to storage
3160	(`direct: true`, plays in a `<video>`, works until `expires_at`, `expires_in` seconds from now, at most 10 minutes;
3161	ask again after that), or else `video` itself. A recording kept as HLS (`hls: true`, most recent runs) is a
3162	playlist: `url` is `video/hls/index.m3u8` on this API, each segment from it too
3163	(hls.js plays it, and `ffmpeg -headers "x-api-key: …" -i <url>` reads it); `native_url` names presigned segments
3164	instead, for a player's own HLS; `video` then answers `303` to the run's page. `videos` places a run's recordings on its timeline, as the run page replays them: each browser's first
3165	frame time (`started_at`, epoch ms) and length, `estimated` when the start time is approximate. Your team
3166	sees the frames and recordings of its runs on the public dataset, test runs and scored runs alike; a private dataset's
3167	(the final run's) stay with the organizers unless they release them.
3168	
3169	A run whose `agent.json` asks for several browsers has a frame and a recording per browser: add `?browser=n`
3170	(1 to 4; browser 1 without it), for example `/v1/runs/$RUN_ID/frame?browser=2` or `/v1/runs/$RUN_ID/video?browser=3`.
3171	`feed` then carries `browsers` and `frames` (each browser's `frame_at` and `frame_hash`), the run lists its
3172	recordings in `videos`, and a share link's response adds `urls`, one per recording. A browser the run does not have
3173	answers `404`; a value other than 1 to 4 answers `400`.
3174	
3175	### Live screen and terminal
3176	
3177	Where available, your team can watch the screen of a run on the public dataset (a test run or a
3178	scored run) live while its agent runs, and a test run's terminal. The run page shows the screens beside the live
3179	logs; an agent or script can ask for the view-only links itself:
3180	
3181	```sh
3182	curl -X POST "$ATIRA_API/v1/runs/$RUN_ID/live/screen" -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN"   # {"url": ..., "expires_at": ...}
3183	curl -X POST "$ATIRA_API/v1/runs/$RUN_ID/live/tty" -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN"      # a test run's raw output
3184	```
3185	
3186	Each browser of a run has its own screen: `POST /v1/runs/$RUN_ID/live/screen?browser=n` (browser 1 without it). A
3187	further browser's viewer may wait a moment for its screen to come up.
3188	
3189	Embed the `url` in an iframe with `referrerpolicy="no-referrer"`. Treat it as a secret: anyone holding it can watch
3190	until it expires, and the viewer ignores input. The same link comes back while it is valid, and it stops working when
3191	the run ends. The terminal shows unredacted output, so it is for test runs and your team only; a run on a private
3192	dataset (the final run) shows its screen to organizers only. `409` means the run is not live (not started, or ended);
3193	`503` means live viewing is unavailable right now (try again later, after `Retry-After` seconds when it is set).

3198	curl "$ATIRA_API/v1/challenges/rfq/leaderboard"
3199	curl "$ATIRA_API/v1/challenges/rfq/leaderboard?dataset=public"     # the public-dataset board
3200	curl "$ATIRA_API/v1/challenges/rfq/stats"
3201	curl "$ATIRA_API/v1/challenges/rfq/activity?limit=30"
3202	curl "$ATIRA_API/v1/challenges/rfq/targets/$TARGET_ID/leaderboard"  # a public evaluation target's board
3203	curl "$ATIRA_API/v1/teams/me" -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN"           # your dashboard

3205	  -H "content-type: application/json" -d "{\"value\": \"$OPENAI_API_KEY\"}"   # a run secret

3209	The leaderboard ranks each team by its best complete submission: eligible first, then higher quality, then the lower
3210	product of cost and time (cost counted as at least $0.01, time as at least 1 s), then the submission ID. Its
3211	`median_*` fields hold the submission's run values. Its `board` says what it ranks:
3212	`{dataset, final, final_live, target_id, label, suite_id, runs}`, with `runs` the sandbox runs per submission.
3213	During the hackathon it is the public-dataset board. Once the organizers publish the final results, the leaderboard
3214	shows them (`dataset` `"private"`, `final` true): every team's latest submission that passed review, ranked the
3215	same way. Each final entry also carries the team's hackathon result: `public_dataset` (`{rank, eligible,
3216	median_quality, median_cost_micro_usd, median_duration_ms}` on the public-dataset board, or null without one) and
3217	`rank_change` (places moved since: positive up, 0 unchanged, null new). `?dataset=public` keeps the public-dataset
3218	board, and `final_live` is true on both.

3220	## Accounts
3221	
3222	With GitHub sign-in, people manage their team in the browser. These endpoints take the `atira_session` cookie,
3223	and writes also need the header `x-atira-csrf` set to the value of the `atira_csrf` cookie. `GET /v1/me` and the
3224	token endpoints also take a personal token. The captain's actions (invites, removing members, revoking the team
3225	key, linking the repository) take a browser session only, never a token.
3226	
3227	- **Invites** are for one GitHub account. The captain enters a teammate's GitHub username
3228	  (`POST /v1/me/team/invites` with `{"login": "octocat"}`) and gets a link `/invites/inv_...` that only that
3229	  account can use, once, within 7 days. Pending invites hold a seat, so a team has at most five members and
3230	  pending invites together. The captain sees them in `GET /v1/me` and revokes one with
3231	  `DELETE /v1/me/team/invites/{invite_id}`. The person invited sees them in `GET /v1/me` (`invites`) and answers
3232	  with `POST /v1/me/invites/{invite_id}/accept` or `/decline`, or joins through the link.
3233	- **Team keys** are not shown with GitHub sign-in: everyone uses their own token, and `GET /v1/me/team/key`
3234	  answers `410`. The captain can still revoke a team key copied before personal sign-in with
3235	  `POST /v1/me/team/key`. Where GitHub sign-in is off, `POST /v1/teams` with `{"name": "..."}` registers a team
3236	  and returns its key once.
